title: Opinions & discussions
goal: Hold your own in a discussion: give your view, agree and disagree without starting a fight, say 'it depends', 'maybe' and 'must be', argue about cricket, and say what someone should have done.
intro:
Indians love a good discussion, whether it's about cricket, politics, prices or whose turn it is to pay. With friends it gets loud and direct; with elders it stays soft and respectful. This unit gives you the phrases that let you join in at both levels: **मेरे हिसाब से** 'the way I see it', **सच कहूँ तो** 'to be honest', **बात तो सही है, लेकिन…** 'fair point, but…'.

The grammar adds three things every argument needs: degrees of certainty (**शायद, हो सकता है, होगा** — maybe, might, must be), the polite way to disagree and to say **'I don't think…'**, and hindsight: **उसे आउट नहीं देना चाहिए था!** 'he shouldn't have been given out!'

grammar.title: Maybe, might, must be: शायद, हो सकता है, होगा
grammar.body:
Hindi has a neat ladder for how sure you are:

**पक्का / ज़रूर** — definitely: वो **पक्का** आएगा
**होगा** — must be, probably is: वो घर पर **होगा** 'he must be at home'
**शायद** — maybe, perhaps: **शायद** वो आए / आएगा
**हो सकता है (कि)** — might, it's possible: **हो सकता है** बारिश **हो**
**चांस कम है** / **मुश्किल है** — unlikely

**होगा = 'must be'.** The future of होना is used for guesses about **now**: वो ऑफ़िस में **होगा** 'he'll be at the office (I suppose)', तुम थक गई **होगी** 'you must be tired'. It agrees: होगा / होगी / होंगे. Add it to a continuous form for 'must be doing': वो रास्ते में आ रहा **होगा** 'he must be on his way'.

**The subjunctive for 'might'.** After **हो सकता है (कि)** and often after **शायद**, the verb goes into the subjunctive (the 'shall I…?' form from units 18 and 26):

मैं जाऊँ · तुम जाओ · वो जाए · हम / आप / वो (pl) जाएँ · and होना → वो **हो**

हो सकता है वो देर से **आए** 'he might come late'. हो सकता है कि मैच कल **हो** 'the match might be tomorrow'. With शायद you can also use the future (शायद वो आएगा) — it sounds a little more likely.

**'Might not'** uses **न** rather than नहीं: हो सकता है वो **न** आए 'he might not come'.

grammar.title: Disagreeing politely and 'I don't think…'
grammar.body:
**'I don't think…'** = **मुझे नहीं लगता कि…** — the नहीं goes on लगता, just like English: **मुझे नहीं लगता कि** वो सच बोल रहा है 'I don't think he's telling the truth'. (You can also say मुझे लगता है कि वो सच **नहीं** बोल रहा, but the first is more natural and softer.) Other openers: **मेरे हिसाब से**, **मेरे ख़याल से** 'in my view', **सच कहूँ तो** 'to be honest', **मेरी राय में** 'in my opinion' (more formal).

**Disagreeing in steps.** Hindi conversation avoids a flat **तुम ग़लत हो** 'you're wrong', especially with elders. Go up the ladder only as far as you need:

1. Agree first: **बात तो सही है, लेकिन…** 'that's true, but…', **हाँ, पर…**
2. Disagree with the idea, not the person: **ऐसा नहीं है** 'it's not like that', **मैं नहीं मानता** 'I'm not convinced'
3. Strong, with friends only: **बिल्कुल नहीं!** 'no way!', **उल्टा, …** 'on the contrary…'

To keep the peace: **निर्भर करता है** 'it depends', **हो सकता है** 'could be', **तुम्हारा पॉइंट समझ गया** 'I get your point', **चलो, इस पर बहस नहीं करते** 'let's not argue about it'.

**The little word तो** adds 'admittedly' to a concession: बात **तो** सही है 'it's true, (I'll give you that)', होशियार **तो** है 'he's clever, sure (but…)'. Expect a लेकिन or पर to follow.

With elders, wrap everything in **जी** and **आप**: **जी, आप सही कह रहे हैं, पर…** 'yes, you're right, but…'.

grammar.title: Should have, could have: चाहिए था, सकता था
grammar.body:
You know **infinitive + चाहिए** for 'should' (unit 9): तुम्हें आराम करना **चाहिए**. Add **था** and it looks back: **should have**.

तुम्हें मुझे पहले बताना **चाहिए था** — you should have told me earlier
मुझे वो मैच देखना **चाहिए था** — I should have watched that match

The person is in the **को** form (मुझे, तुम्हें, उसे, हमें, कप्तान को). **Negative:** put **नहीं** before the infinitive: उसे आउट **नहीं** देना चाहिए था 'he shouldn't have been given out (lit. one shouldn't have given him out)'.

**Agreement.** In careful Hindi the infinitive and था agree with the object, as with मुझे … है (unit 25): हमें पहले बॉलिंग **लेनी** चाहिए **थी** (बॉलिंग is f). In fast speech you'll also hear लेना चाहिए था.

**Could have** = stem + **सकता था / सकती थी / सकते थे**: हम यह मैच जीत **सकते थे** 'we could have won this match', तुम आ **सकते थे** 'you could have come'. It agrees with the subject and never takes ने.

These are the backbone of every post-match discussion and every 'I told you so'.

lines.speaker: Simran
lines.native: सच कहूँ तो, मुझे नहीं लगता कि टॉस से इतना फ़र्क़ पड़ता है।

lines.speaker: Arjun

lines.roman: paṛtā hai! rāt ko os ātī hai, phir boliṅg mushkil ho jātī hai.
lines.en: It does! At night the dew comes down, and then bowling gets hard.

lines.speaker: Simran

lines.roman: bāt to sahī hai, lekin yah pich bhī ajīb-sī hai. nirbhar kartā hai.

lines.speaker: Kabir
lines.en: Oh, forget the toss! Look, a six!

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.native: क्या शॉट था! यह लड़का कमाल का खिलाड़ी है।
lines.roman: kyā shoṭ thā! yah laṛkā kamāl kā khilāṛī hai.
lines.en: What a shot! This kid is an amazing player.

lines.speaker: Simran
lines.native: हो सकता है हम अब भी जीत जाएँ।

lines.speaker: Kabir
lines.native: शायद। पर बारिश हुई तो… पता नहीं।
lines.roman: shāyad. par bārish huī to… patā nahīṃ.
lines.en: Maybe. But if it rains… who knows.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.native: बारिश नहीं होगी, मैंने ऐप पर देखा है।
lines.roman: bārish nahīṃ hogī, maiṃne aip par dekhā hai.

lines.speaker: Simran
lines.native: तुम्हारे ऐप ने पिछली बार भी यही कहा था!
lines.roman: tumhāre aip ne pichhlī bār bhī yahī kahā thā!

lines.en: Ha ha! Come on, stop arguing and watch the match!

culture: Among friends, discussion in Hindi is loud, fast and full of mock outrage (**पागल है क्या?** 'are you mad?') — it's a sport, not a fight, and **यार** softens almost anything. With elders and in-laws it's different: you agree first (**जी, आप सही कह रहे हैं**), then add your **पर…** gently, and you often let them have the last word. **Cricket** is the safest topic in India: everyone has an opinion on the captain, the toss and the umpire, and IPL season fills every chai stall with experts. Football has a big following too, especially in Kerala, Goa and the Northeast, and among Premier League fans in the cities. **Politics** and **religion** are much hotter: people talk about them a lot, but wait until you know someone well, and **चलो, इस पर बहस नहीं करते** is always a graceful exit. **महँगाई** (prices) and, in Delhi every winter, **प्रदूषण**, are things everyone agrees to complain about. Notice how English words — **point, depend, chance, idea** — slip into Hindi arguments mid-sentence; that's completely normal.

lessons.title: Giving your view

tip.title: मेरे हिसाब से — giving your view
tip.body:
- Start softly: **मेरे हिसाब से** / **मेरे ख़याल से** 'in my view', **सच कहूँ तो** 'to be honest'.
- 'I don't think…' = **मुझे नहीं लगता कि** …
- Ask: **तुम्हें क्या लगता है?** · **आपकी क्या राय है?**
- **ना** at the end invites agreement: सही है **ना**?
tip.pattern: मेरे हिसाब से … · मुझे नहीं लगता कि …

lessons.title: Disagreeing without a fight

tip.title: Disagreeing politely
tip.body:
- Agree first, then disagree: **बात तो सही है, लेकिन…** 'fair point, but…'.
- Softer than **तुम ग़लत हो**: **ऐसा नहीं है** · **मैं नहीं मानता**.
- Strong — friends only: **बिल्कुल नहीं!** · **उल्टा, …** 'on the contrary'.
- To end it: **चलो, इस पर बहस नहीं करते**.

tip.title: शायद, हो सकता है, होगा
tip.body:
- **शायद** + subjunctive or future: शायद वो **आए** / **आएगा**.
- **हो सकता है (कि)** + subjunctive = might: हो सकता है बारिश **हो**.
- **होगा / होगी** = must be: वो घर पर **होगा**, तुम थक गई **होगी**.
- 'Might not' takes **न**: हो सकता है वो **न** आए.

sentences.roman: ho saktā hai vo āj der se āye.
sentences.en: He might come late today.

sentences.native: वो अभी ऑफ़िस में होगा, बाद में फ़ोन करो।
sentences.roman: vo abhī ofis meṃ hogā, bād meṃ fon karo.
sentences.en: He'll be at the office now, call later.

sentences.native: तुम थक गई होगी, आराम करो।
sentences.roman: tum thak gaī hogī, ārām karo.
sentences.en: You must be tired, have a rest. (to a woman)

sentences.native: जीतने का चांस बहुत कम है।
sentences.roman: jītne kā chāns bahut kam hai.
sentences.en: The chance of winning is very small.

sentences.native: हो सकता है कि वो सच बोल रहा हो।
sentences.roman: ho saktā hai ki vo sach bol rahā ho.
sentences.en: He might be telling the truth.

sentences.native: निर्भर करता है कि कितने लोग आते हैं।
sentences.roman: nirbhar kartā hai ki kitne log āte haiṃ.
sentences.en: It depends how many people come.

sentences.native: क्या फ़र्क़ पड़ता है? सब ठीक हो जाएगा।
sentences.roman: kyā farq paṛtā hai? sab ṭhīk ho jāyegā.
sentences.en: What difference does it make? It'll all be fine.

sentences.native: शायद तुम सही हो।
sentences.roman: shāyad tum sahī ho.
sentences.en: Maybe you're right.

sentences.native: वो रास्ते में होगी, ट्रैफ़िक बहुत है।
sentences.roman: vo rāste meṃ hogī, ṭraifik bahut hai.
sentences.en: She must be on her way, there's a lot of traffic.

sentences.native: हो सकता है, पर मैं पक्का नहीं कह सकता।
sentences.roman: ho saktā hai, par maiṃ pakkā nahīṃ kah saktā.
sentences.en: Could be, but I can't say for sure. (man)

sentences.native: चांस है कि मैच कल हो जाए।
sentences.roman: chāns hai ki maich kal ho jāye.
sentences.en: There's a chance the match will happen tomorrow.

sentences.native: आज भारत का मैच है, साथ में देखें?
sentences.roman: āj bhārat kā maich hai, sāth meṃ dekheṃ?
sentences.en: India's playing today, shall we watch together?

sentences.native: हमारी टीम पहले बैटिंग कर रही है।
sentences.roman: hamārī ṭīm pahle baiṭiṅg kar rahī hai.
sentences.en: Our team is batting first.

sentences.native: अरे, वो आउट हो गया! इतनी जल्दी?
sentences.roman: are, vo āuṭ ho gayā! itnī jaldī?
sentences.en: Oh no, he's out! So soon?

sentences.native: क्या छक्का था!
sentences.roman: kyā chhakkā thā!
sentences.en: What a six!

sentences.native: अंपायर ने ग़लत आउट दिया।
sentences.roman: ampāyar ne ġalat āuṭ diyā.
sentences.en: The umpire gave him out wrongly.

sentences.native: मैं कभी स्टेडियम में मैच देखने नहीं गया।
sentences.roman: maiṃ kabhī sṭeḍiyam meṃ maich dekhne nahīṃ gayā.
sentences.en: I've never been to a match at the stadium. (man)

sentences.native: आज हमारी बैटिंग बहुत अच्छी चल रही है।
sentences.roman: āj hamārī baiṭiṅg bahut achchhī chal rahī hai.
sentences.en: Our batting is going really well today.

sentences.native: स्कोर क्या है? कितने आउट हुए?
sentences.roman: skor kyā hai? kitne āuṭ hue?
sentences.en: What's the score? How many are out?

sentences.native: अभी कौन-सी टीम जीत रही है?
sentences.roman: abhī kaun-sī ṭīm jīt rahī hai?
sentences.en: Which team is winning right now?

sentences.native: लगता है आज हम हार जाएँगे।
sentences.roman: lagtā hai āj ham hār jāyeṃge.
sentences.en: Looks like we're going to lose today.

lessons.title: They should have…

tip.title: चाहिए था — should have
tip.body:
- **infinitive + चाहिए था** = should have: तुम्हें पहले **बताना चाहिए था**.
- Negative: उसे आउट **नहीं** देना चाहिए था.
- The infinitive and था can agree with the object: बॉलिंग **लेनी** चाहिए **थी** (f).
- Could have = **सकता था**: हम जीत **सकते थे**!

new: उसे आउट नहीं देना चाहिए था!

sentences.native: टॉस जीतकर हमें पहले बॉलिंग लेनी चाहिए थी।
sentences.roman: ṭos jītkar hameṃ pahle boliṅg lenī chāhiye thī.
sentences.en: After winning the toss we should have bowled first.

sentences.native: तुम्हें मुझे पहले बताना चाहिए था!
sentences.roman: tumheṃ mujhe pahle batānā chāhiye thā!
sentences.en: You should have told me earlier!

sentences.native: हम यह मैच जीत सकते थे!
sentences.roman: ham yah maich jīt sakte the!
sentences.en: We could have won this match!

sentences.native: अंपायर को ध्यान से देखना चाहिए था।
sentences.roman: ampāyar ko dhyān se dekhnā chāhiye thā.
sentences.en: The umpire should have looked more carefully.

sentences.native: आज पूरी टीम बहुत बुरा खेली।
sentences.roman: āj pūrī ṭīm bahut burā khelī.
sentences.en: The whole team played really badly today.

sentences.native: मुझे वो मैच देखना चाहिए था, सब कह रहे हैं बहुत बढ़िया था।
sentences.roman: mujhe vo maich dekhnā chāhiye thā, sab kah rahe haiṃ bahut baṛhiyā thā.
sentences.en: I should have watched that match, everyone says it was brilliant.

sentences.native: तुम्हें इतनी देर तक नहीं जागना चाहिए था।
sentences.roman: tumheṃ itnī der tak nahīṃ jāgnā chāhiye thā.
sentences.en: You shouldn't have stayed up so late.

sentences.native: यह बिल्कुल ग़लत है, उसे आउट नहीं देना चाहिए था!
sentences.roman: yah bilkul ġalat hai, use āuṭ nahīṃ denā chāhiye thā!
sentences.en: That's totally wrong, he shouldn't have been given out!

sentences.native: यह बकवास बहाना है, तुम आ सकते थे।
sentences.roman: yah bakvās bahānā hai, tum ā sakte the.
sentences.en: That's a rubbish excuse, you could have come.

sentences.native: टॉस से कोई फ़र्क़ नहीं पड़ता, बॉलिंग ख़राब थी।
sentences.roman: ṭos se koī farq nahīṃ paṛtā, boliṅg xarāb thī.
sentences.en: The toss doesn't matter, the bowling was bad.

sentences.native: आजकल हर जगह महँगाई की बात हो रही है।
sentences.roman: ājkal har jagah mahaṃgāī kī bāt ho rahī hai.
sentences.en: Everyone is talking about prices these days.

sentences.native: दिल्ली में सर्दियों में प्रदूषण बहुत बढ़ जाता है।
sentences.roman: Dillī meṃ sardiyoṃ meṃ pradūṣaṇ bahut baṛh jātā hai.
sentences.en: In Delhi, pollution gets really bad in winter.

sentences.native: मैं राजनीति पर बात नहीं करता, घर में बहस हो जाती है।
sentences.roman: maiṃ rājnīti par bāt nahīṃ kartā, ghar meṃ bahas ho jātī hai.
sentences.en: I don't talk politics, it turns into an argument at home. (man)

sentences.native: सरकार को प्रदूषण के बारे में कुछ करना चाहिए।
sentences.roman: sarkār ko pradūṣaṇ ke bāre meṃ kuchh karnā chāhiye.
sentences.en: The government should do something about pollution.

sentences.native: सब नेता एक जैसे होते हैं।
sentences.roman: sab netā ek jaise hote haiṃ.
sentences.en: Politicians are all the same.

sentences.native: हो सकता है, पर सब नहीं।
sentences.roman: ho saktā hai, par sab nahīṃ.
sentences.en: Maybe, but not all of them.

sentences.native: अगले साल चुनाव हैं, तुम वोट दोगे?
sentences.roman: agle sāl chunāv haiṃ, tum voṭ doge?
sentences.en: There are elections next year, are you going to vote?

sentences.native: सरकार को पहले ही कुछ करना चाहिए था।
sentences.roman: sarkār ko pahle hī kuchh karnā chāhiye thā.
sentences.en: The government should have done something long ago.

sentences.native: महँगाई इतनी बढ़ गई है कि सब्ज़ी भी महँगी हो गई।
sentences.roman: mahaṃgāī itnī baṛh gaī hai ki sabzī bhī mahaṃgī ho gaī.
sentences.en: Prices have gone up so much that even vegetables are expensive now.

sentences.native: तुमने आज की ख़बर पढ़ी? नेता जी फिर से पार्टी बदल रहे हैं!
sentences.roman: tumne āj kī xabar paṛhī? netā jī phir se pārṭī badal rahe haiṃ!
sentences.en: Did you see today's news? Our politician friend is switching parties again!
